Empirical Research Plan ― “Capital Assistance, Bank Risk-Taking, and Default Risk during the 2008-09 Crisis”

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Main strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with staggered treatment dates, implemented as a dynamic event-study DID (Sun & Abraham 2021 / Callaway & Sant’Anna 2021 estimator).

Why DID is appropriate
• Treatment (receipt of CPP capital) occurred to some but not all eligible banks, and the timing varies (2008Q4–2009Q2).  
• We observe multiple pre- and post-quarters (2006Q1-2010Q4) for both treated and never-treated banks, allowing us to compare changes over time.  
• The institutional process (regulator screening + Treasury decision) generated quasi-experimental variation that is plausibly orthogonal to within-bank shocks in the very short run, satisfying the DID parallel-trends logic better than a pure cross-section.  
• Dynamic DID lets us: (i) test for pre-trend violations, (ii) plot the trajectory of risk-taking, and (iii) account for heterogeneous treatment timing without imposing equal effects across cohorts.

Supplementary analyses
• Propensity-score-weighted DID (doubly-robust) to improve covariate balance.  
• IV-DID robustness using “regulator backlog” (share of earlier applications approved by the same supervisor in the same month) as an instrument for approval, further mitigating endogenous approval concerns.  
• Event-study in stock-market implied default risk around announcement dates as external validation.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable
Treat_i,t = 1 if bank i has received CPP funds by quarter t; 0 otherwise.  
Treatment date τ_i = first quarter in which capital is disbursed (hand-collected). Once treated, banks remain treated (absorbing).

Control group (counterfactual)
• Primary: Eligible banks that never receive CPP funds within the sample window (2006-2010).  
• Secondary robustness: (a) Banks that applied but were rejected, (b) Banks that accepted but repaid early, coded as treated only while funds outstanding.

Event time
k = quarter t – τ_i. We include k = −12,…,+8; omit k = −1 as the reference.

No RDD running variable is used in the main design, but Camels composite (1–5) will be explored as an RD placebo.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of CPP funding, treated and control banks would have exhibited similar evolution in risk-taking.  
  Plausibility: Many pre-crisis quarters are observed; dynamic-DID pre-coefficients can be inspected. Propensity weighting and bank FE further mitigate differences.

A2. No anticipatory effects: Banks did not sharply change risk before regulators/Treasury actually approved funding.  
  Plausibility: Approval decisions were confidential and uncertain; most approvals announced days before disbursement. We will check k = −3, −2 coefficients.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): One bank’s CPP receipt does not directly change another’s risk through competitive spillovers.  
  Plausibility: Some contagion possible in concentrated markets; we will control for county*quarter housing shocks and include MSA-level treated share interacted with time as robustness.

A4. Common shocks: Macro conditions that coincide with the crisis affect all banks similarly and are soaked up by quarter FEs.

A5. Exogeneity of disbursement timing: Conditional on observable fundamentals and regulator fixed effects, the exact quarter of funding is not driven by unobserved risk shocks.  
  Plausibility: Application queue length largely outside banks’ control; regulator workflow differences can be accounted for with supervisor*quarter FEs.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Threat 1: Non-random selection into application/approval (adverse selection).
  • Mitigation: (i) Include applicant-only sample so selection occurs on approval only. (ii) Propensity-score weighting using 2007 characteristics. (iii) IV robustness with “regulator backlog”.

Threat 2: Differential exposure to local housing/economic shocks.
  • Mitigation: Control for county-level house-price changes, unemployment, and foreclosure notices (weighted by branch network); include state*quarter FEs.

Threat 3: Treatment effect heterogeneity with staggered DID biasing TWFE estimators.
  • Mitigation: Use interaction-weighted estimators (Sun & Abraham) that are robust to heterogeneous treatment effects, plus report Goodman-Bacon weights.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R CODE OUTLINE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# Install/load packages
libs <- c("tidyverse","fixest","did","MatchIt","data.table")
lapply(libs, require, character.only = TRUE)

# 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
bank   <- fread("bank_quarterly.csv")        # Call Report vars
cpp    <- fread("cpp_events.csv")            # application & disbursement dates
county <- fread("county_macro.csv")          # housing & labor vars

# 2. Merge & construct panel ----------------------------------------------
panel <- bank %>% 
  left_join(cpp,  by = "cert") %>%           # 'cert' = FDIC cert number
  mutate(t = as.yearqtr(date),
         treat_date = as.yearqtr(cpp_first_disbursement),
         ever_treat = !is.na(treat_date),
         treat = ifelse(ever_treat & t >= treat_date, 1, 0),
         rel_time = ifelse(ever_treat, as.integer((t - treat_date)*4), NA)) %>% 
  left_join(county, by = c("county_fips","t"))

# 3. Preferred specification (dynamic DID) -------------------------------
es <- feols(risk_outcome ~ sunab(treat_date, t) + 
              log_assets + roa + tier1_cap + county_hpchg + county_unemp |
              cert + t,       # bank FE, quarter FE
            cluster = ~cert,
            data = panel)

# 4. Display results & plot event study ----------------------------------
etable(es, se = "cluster")

iplot(es, pt.col = "blue", ref.line = -1, main = "Dynamic DID: CPP Effect on Risk")

# 5. Robustness: Propensity-score weighted DID -----------------------------
# Pre-treatment covariates from 2007
covars <- c("log_assets_2007","roa_2007","tier1_2007","nonperf_2007")
ps <- matchit(ever_treat ~ ., data = panel %>% filter(t=="2007 Q3") %>% select(ever_treat, all_of(covars)),
              method = "nearest")
wts <- match.data(ps)$weights
panel <- panel %>% mutate(w = wts[match(cert, match.data(ps)$cert)])

es_w <- feols(risk_outcome ~ treat + log_assets + roa + tier1_cap |
                cert + t, data = panel, weights = ~w, cluster=~cert)
etable(list(Base=es, PSM=es_w), se="cluster")

# 6. IV robustness: regulator backlog instrument --------------------------
panel <- panel %>% mutate(backlog = regulator_monthly_share_prev_approved)
iv <- feols(risk_outcome ~ 1 | treat ~ backlog,
            data = panel, cluster = ~cert | ~cert)   # fixest 2SLS syntax
```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. EXPECTED RESULTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Economic intuition: An explicit government capital backstop lowers banks’ private cost of failure, creating moral hazard. I expect:

• Lending: a relative shift toward riskier mortgages (higher loan-to-value, lower FICO) and toward lower-rated syndicated loans.  
• Securities: higher share of non-agency MBS and corporate bonds.  
• Accounting asset risk (RWAs/assets): ↑ by 1–2 p.p. within one year (baseline ≈ 65 %).  
• Market-implied default risk (e.g., KMV EDF): little change or small decline, because higher capital buffers partly offset riskier assets.

Hence the average CPP bank will show +3–5 % s.d. increase in risk-taking metrics but near-zero effect on distance-to-default.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Clear treatment definition and timing ………………… 1  
C2: Parallel pre-trends visually & statistically supported … 0.8  
C3: No interference/spillovers ……………………………………… 0.6  
C4: Correct model for staggered timing (SA estimator) …… 1  
C5: Robustness to alternative controls/specifications …… 0.8  

Total ≈ 4.2 / 5 → Reasonably credible, but spillovers and residual selection remain areas to watch.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
